page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Award-winning!
title: Award-winning!
topic: Language to use when accepting an award
description:
It's the end of a busy day at the International Plastics Convention, and that means it's awards time! Tip Top Trading are up for the most prestigious prize – the Plastic Innovation of the Year award – but will they win?
This episode focuses on the language that you might use if you win an award and have to make an acceptance speech.
phrases: Ladies and gentlemen, on behalf of everyone at Tip Top Trading, thank you for our award.
Our company is at the forefront of plastic innovation.
This award is a real boost for everyone working at the company.
This award really means a lot to us.

listening_challenge.question: What product does Tip Top Trading win its plastic innovation award for?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to English at Work. Paul, Anna and Tom are at an important International Plastics Conference. It’s been a busy day of networking but the big boss from America, Mr Socrates, has told Paul some bad news. Before he tells the team, there is an important award to be won – the Plastic Innovation of the Year award. Will Tip Top Trading win it?
I hope you've written your acceptance speech Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes, I'm just doing it now.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You've left it a bit late.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I've been so busy and now I'm really struggling. I don't know what to write.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, don't forget to say "On behalf of everyone at Tip Top Trading, thank you for our award". Or, you could say "our company is at the forefront of plastic innovation". Tell the audience "this award is a real boost for everyone working at the company". Say that and you'll be fine.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: …working at the company. Good, got it. Thanks. Oh hi Tom, how have you got on?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Great great. I've been hanging out with some of our clients – keeping them sweet, you know what I mean?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Err, I don't actually know. But I've had some success. Oh, here comes Paul.  Hi Paul.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh hello. Having a good day?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes, we're just talking about our success – let's hope we win that Plastic Innovation of the Year award, eh?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh yes... let's hope so. Although that means I've got to read out that speech you wrote for me. Public speaking is not really one of my things.

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: Ladies and gentlemen, please take your seats for our special award ceremony.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK, here's your speech Paul.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: We've got to win first.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Shhh shhh. Listen!

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: Thank you everyone for attending this year's conference. As you know, the highlight of the day is announcing the winner of our Plastic Innovation Award. So, without further ado, let's find out who this year's winner is. It is… Tip Top Trading for their Imperial Lemon.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Hey, that's us. We've actually won!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh crumbs. I suppose I'd better do my speech now.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah… go on Paul you can do it!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: OK, right. Whooah… ouch.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh no. Paul's tripped over that chair.

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: Is there anyone from Tip Top Trading here?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Anna, you'll have to do the speech – you did write it after all.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What me?! I can't.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Go on. You'll be fine and besides I'm no good at public speaking.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yes you can do it Anna! Just start by saying 'ladies and gentlemen'.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, if I have to. Erm… ladies and gentlemen. On behalf of everyone at Tip Top Trading, thank you for our award… our company is at the forefront of plastic innovation.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Erm… thanks Tom. This award is a real boost for everyone working at the company. We pride ourselves on innovation, quality and err… plastic fruit. And coming soon, we'll be launching a new plastic aubergine.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Ow, my big toe!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: So thank you everyone, this really means a lot to us.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Brilliant Anna.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes splendid. Well done Anna.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well done indeed. Anna saved the day again by making that speech. She sounded confident and genuinely happy about getting the award. Here's a reminder of some of things she said:
Ladies and gentlemen, on behalf of everyone at Tip Top Trading, thank you for our award.
Our company is at the forefront of plastic innovation.
This award is a real boost for everyone working at the company.
This award really means a lot to us.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Are you OK now Paul?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes, sorry, that was rather unfortunate and a bit embarrassing too, but… hold on… what's happening now?

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: Ladies and gentlemen, before you go, we have one more award to present.

transcript.speaker: Everyone
transcript.text: Oooh!

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: We have a special award. 'Employee of the Year'. This recognises someone’s achievements and contribution to the plastics industry.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: At last, I've been recognised.

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: Please welcome Brad Socrates from Tip Top Trading International to award the prize.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Out the way. Where's the Goddamn envelope?  OK, right, and the award goes to… Anna from Tip Top Trading.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Me? Bbbut I…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Go on Anna. You deserve it. Go and make another speech!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thank you everyone – this is amazing.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: This girl is amazing. In just one year she has risen from an apprentice to a champion. It's great to have her on board. I think we should talk about your salary later hey?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Can things get any better for Anna? I think they can. Join us again soon for more English at Work. Bye.
